title: The gradient of a curve
query_text: how do you find the gradient of a curve

modules.title: From a secant to a tangent

segments.narration_intent: Secants from P(1, 1) on y = x^2 get closer to the tangent at P as Q moves towards P, and their gradients approach 2.
Sliding the tangent along y = x^2 shows that the gradient of a curve changes from point to point.

narration: Here is the curve y equals x squared. Unlike a straight line, it gets steeper as it goes, so we cannot use one rise over run for the whole curve.
Mark the point P at 1, 1, and a second point Q further along the curve. The straight line through them is called a secant, and its gradient is 4.
Now slide Q closer to P. The secant gradient drops to 3, then 2.5, then 2.1.
As Q reaches P, the secant becomes the tangent at P. Its gradient is 2, and that is the gradient of the curve at P.
Here is y equals x squared again, this time from minus 3 to 3.
At x equals minus 2, the tangent slopes downwards. Its gradient is minus 4.
Slide the tangent to the right. The gradient rises through 0 at the bottom of the curve, and at x equals 2 it is 4. A curve has a different gradient at every point.

modules.title: The gradient function of x squared

segments.narration_intent: The gradient of the secant from x to x + h on y = x^2 simplifies to 2x + h, which becomes 2x as h shrinks to 0.

narration: Take any point x on the curve y equals x squared, and a second point h further along. The gradient of the secant is the change in y, x plus h all squared minus x squared, over the change in x, which is h.
Expanding the bracket, the x squared terms cancel, leaving 2 x h plus h squared, all over h.
Dividing by h gives 2 x plus h. As h shrinks to 0, this becomes 2 x. So the derivative of x squared is 2 x, and at x equals 1 the gradient is 2, just as the secants showed.

segments.narration_intent: On y = x^3 - 3x the tangent flattens out at x = 1, where the gradient is 0: a stationary point.
Setting the derivative 3x^2 - 3 equal to 0 finds the stationary points at x = 1 and x = -1.

narration: Here is the curve y equals x cubed minus 3 x. It rises, turns, falls, and then rises again.
At x equals minus 2, the tangent is steep, with a gradient of 9.
Slide it to the right. The gradient falls, and at x equals 1 the tangent is flat: the gradient is 0. A point where the gradient is 0 is called a stationary point.
To find every stationary point, set the derivative, 3 x squared minus 3, equal to 0.
Add 3 to both sides: 3 x squared equals 3.
Divide by 3: x squared equals 1. So x is 1 or minus 1. The curve has two stationary points, one at each turn.
